<description>
Previously, signing was assuming that MuSig2 information from the given `SigningProvider` was all from the descriptor that is relevant to the input being signed. However, in both `descriptorprocesspsbt` and `utxoupdatepsbt`, this is not true as information from all provided descriptors is put into the `SigningProvider` that is passed to `SignTaproot`. Consequently, if one of the given descriptors involved a MuSig2, the MuSig2 information would be accidentally added to the `SignatureData` which results in those fields appearing in the resulting PSBT.

Both the filling of aggregate pubkey information as well as participant BIP 32 derivation paths is moved to after the aggregate pubkey check inside of `SignMuSig2`. This ensures that information about only the aggregates pertaining to the particular script being signed are included in the resulting PSBT.

Fixes #36323
</description>

[2026-10-01] c:5940991797 comment by fametrano (contributor):
Tested bca240a0e0: the fix works. ACK once the assert polespinasa flagged is fixed.

I ran `utxoupdatepsbt` and `descriptorprocesspsbt` on master and on this PR with the issue's descriptor and four variants: musig() in a leaf, ranged participants, a BIP328-derived aggregate, and a key in two aggregates. On master a participant gets every leaf hash. With the PR it gets only the hashes of leaves that contain it or an aggregate it belongs to.

@Zeegaths if your descriptor has the issue's shape, `tr(musig(A,B),pk(C))`, the two keys that lose the hash are A and B. They are only in the key path, so the empty lists are what the issue asks for.
[2026-10-01] rc:4160674221 inline on test/functional/rpc_psbt.py by fametrano (contributor):
Agreed: `decodepsbt` writes `musig2_participant_pubkeys`, so the assert as written can never fail. With eab30978ea reverted the unrelated aggregate is back, and the test still passes. With your suggestion it fails on that assert, and it passes on the PR.
